title: Rav Tuvi bar Kisni
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He was Shmuel’s student, as Hyman says we always find “Rav Tuvi bar Kisna said that Shmuel said,” as in Yevamot 40b, Ketubot 64a, Nedarim 12b, Bava Batra 19b and Menachot 41a. There at 70a, “Rav Tavyomi bar Kisna said that Shmuel said,” Hyman proposes reading Rav Tuvi bar Kisna, according to Dikdukei Soferim’s reading. There at 76b, “Rav Tuvi bar Kasna said that Shmuel said,” Hyman proposes reading bar Kisna. In Eruvin 104b, “Rav Tavi bar Kisna said that Shmuel said,” Hyman proposes reading Rav Tivi, and so it is in Tosafot on Sotah 20b, s.v. Lo.

notes.text: The heading’s Kisni (קיסני) is preserved in the title, while Kisna, Kasna, Tuvi, Tavyomi, Tavi and Tivi remain as the supplied body’s meaningful variants. Saved Davidson Menachot 70a/76b and Eruvin 104b retain several of those forms. The proposed corrections and always assertion remain Hyman’s, not global name harmonization.

The directly inspected Menachot 70a and Eruvin 104b occurrences read Tavyomi and Tavi respectively. The exact Dikdukei Soferim and Tosafot readings quoted here have not been independently inspected; those corrections remain Hyman’s.
